uvMaskTool.title: Iyan-Kim UV Mask Tool
uvMaskTool.copy: A Unity editor tool for selecting UV islands from a Renderer's Material Slot and exporting the selected region as a PNG mask texture. It lets you build precise UV masks directly inside Unity without repainting UV regions manually in an external tool.

cards.title: Best For
cards.body: VRChat avatars, outfits, props, and modular meshes with multiple material slots and UV islands that need mask textures.

cards.title: UV Selection Workflow
cards.body: Reads only the triangles that belong to the selected Material Slot, lets you select islands or faces, and exports the result directly as a PNG mask.

cards.title: Preview and Export
cards.body: Combines UV preview, texture overlay, wireframe, Scene View highlighting, resolution presets, padding, and anti-aliasing in a single workflow.

meta.body: Designed for Unity 2022.3+, MeshRenderer or SkinnedMeshRenderer targets, meshes with usable UVs, and renderers that expose one or more Material Slots.

image.alt: UV Mask Tool English UI screenshot
image.caption: You can assign a renderer, choose the target Material Slot, preview UVs, configure export settings, and write the selected area to a PNG mask from one window.

sections.title: Key Features
items: Detects UV islands from only the submesh triangles used by the selected Material Slot.
Automatically detects available UV channels for the selected slot.
Supports UV preview, zoom, panning, wireframe display, and texture overlay preview.
Supports both island-based selection and individual face selection.
Can highlight the matching mesh triangles in the Scene View.
Exports PNG masks with resolution presets, custom resolution, alpha, padding, and anti-aliasing controls.
Supports Korean, English, and Japanese UI, and stores language settings in EditorPrefs.

sections.title: Requirements
items: Unity 2022.3 or newer
MeshRenderer or SkinnedMeshRenderer
A mesh with usable UV data
A renderer with one or more material slots
Editor-only usage

sections.title: Basic Usage
items: Open Iyan-Kim > Tools > UV Island Mask Generator.
Assign a MeshRenderer or SkinnedMeshRenderer in the renderer field.
Choose the Material Slot that should define the mask source area.
Select the desired UV islands or individual faces in the preview.
Configure resolution, alpha, colors, padding, and anti-aliasing.
Click Export PNG to save the selected UV region as a mask texture.

entries.title: Renderer / Material Slot
entries.body: Defines the working mesh target and the specific Material Slot whose submesh triangles should be scanned.

entries.title: UV Preview / Preview Texture
entries.body: Shows the UV layout for the selected slot and lets you overlay either a manually assigned Texture2D or the current material's main texture.

entries.title: Selection Mode / Select All / Invert / Clear
entries.body: Lets you switch between island mode and face mode, then quickly manage selection state with select-all, invert, or clear actions.

entries.title: Scene View Highlight
entries.body: Highlights the actual mesh triangles that correspond to the selected UV region directly inside the Scene View.

entries.title: Export Settings
entries.body: Supports preset resolutions from 256 to 4096, custom resolution up to 8192, alpha output, background and selection colors, padding, and anti-aliasing options.

sections.title: Tips
items: Choose the Material Slot first so the correct material region is isolated before selecting islands.
Island mode is fastest on clean UV layouts, while face mode is useful for small or irregular areas.
Preview Texture makes it much easier to confirm what region is being selected on top of the actual texture.
High resolutions combined with SSAA 4x can consume a lot of memory, so large exports should be handled carefully.
This is especially useful for outfit pieces, ornaments, skin zones, or shader masks on VRChat avatars.

entries.title: The mesh cannot be found
entries.body: For MeshRenderer targets, verify that a MeshFilter exists on the same GameObject and that sharedMesh is assigned. For SkinnedMeshRenderer, make sure sharedMesh is connected correctly.

entries.title: The Material Slot list is empty
entries.body: Check that the renderer actually has material slots and that the selected submesh contains valid triangles. Empty submeshes may be skipped.

entries.title: No usable UV channels are detected
entries.body: Make sure the mesh contains UV data and that the selected Material Slot triangles have non-zero UV area.

entries.title: UV islands are not generated
entries.body: Detection can fail if UVs overlap heavily or if only zero-area triangles exist. Try another Material Slot or review the automatically detected UV channel results.

entries.title: Export PNG is disabled
entries.body: Confirm that a renderer and Material Slot are selected, at least one island or face is chosen, and the resolution value stays between 1 and 8192.
